pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented as three to four sessions a week of 30-45 minutes, core and stability framed directly at his back problem — 'super good for your core. Every movement uses your core a lot. It's very good for your stability, which helps you with your back a lot' — with mobility positioned as the joints, tendons, ligaments and fascia layer, 'with your back specifically, it's going to be very, very important.' He agreed without questions or enthusiasm: 'Yeah, I think so' and later 'it sounds good. It sounds like what I would like to do, for sure.' No mechanics questions and no tie back to his own goal.

He had already specified what he wanted before it was presented — 'I'm not really looking for a diet either. I'd rather just figure out the best way to eat for my body and for the type of training I want to do so that I can be consistent' — and the presentation matched it closely: not restrictive, guidelines rather than gram weights, recomposition rather than rapid loss so he does not repeat the keto muscle loss. He raised no objection and asked nothing further. Notably the rep explicitly addressed the keto failure mode without the prospect having to push.

The pillar that was already sold before it was presented. He volunteered the whole case for it unprompted: 'coaching in general has been something that's a little easier for me to think about doing because going and doing group classes has always been easier for me because I don't have to think about it. I'll go in there and I'll work my butt off in class, but I hate coming up with — I don't have the mental capacity with everything else I've got going on in life to come up with a plan.' The rep mirrored it back as holding him to 'the version of you who is the role model for his kids', which the prospect accepted without hesitation.

anchors.raw: We've got a few kettlebells at the house. We just recently got a gym membership, mainly just because my kids are all at the age where they can start going to the gym by themselves anyways
anchors.note: He has just bought the cheap solution — a family gym membership and bells at home — and named group classes as the format that has historically worked best for him. The paid coaching has to beat a live class he can attend for a monthly fee, and the rep never drew that comparison. Also mildly supportive: it shows an active willingness to spend on fitness for the household.

anchors.raw: I got back to 190 just by, you know, eating like keto, doing kind of the keto thing for a while. I dropped like four, almost 40 pounds doing that and not really even working out that much.
anchors.note: He has already produced a 40 lb loss for free, which is a real ceiling on what weight loss alone is worth to him. The rep handled this better than on comparable calls by attacking the quality of that result rather than the result itself — positioning recomposition against muscle loss — which converts the anchor into a reason to buy.

anchors.raw: 70% roughly of our clients are business owners. So we're very, very used to framing it in a way that you can write it off as well. So if you need help with that, we'll help you write it off. It's always good when it's almost free. It's not free, but in a way.
anchors.note: A rep-created supportive anchor that reframes $6,000 as effectively discounted by tax treatment. Commercially effective and it landed — the prospect immediately started thinking in business terms. It is also unqualified tax advice offered by a fitness sales rep with an offer to help structure it, which is flagged separately.

anchors.raw: It'll be, uh, cheaper than surgery in 10 years if you needed it.
anchors.note: Rep-created, deployed pre-emptively before any number was quoted, and it worked — the prospect had already framed the purchase against future healthcare cost himself. Worth noting that it is a health prediction delivered by a salesperson to a man with an untreated recurrent back problem.

unmet_demand.want: Training he can genuinely do anywhere, so that travel and vacations stop breaking the routine — the specific failure mode he identified as his own root cause, with a Florida trip already booked for the end of summer
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He named it as the thing that must be solved and the rep never answered it. The programme does have travel routines — this rep described them in detail on another call in the same week — and here he moved straight from the diagnosis to the philosophy pitch without ever saying 'here is what your week in Florida looks like'. The single clearest missed alignment on the call.

unmet_demand.want: Something his 13-year-old son can train alongside him, since homeschooling leaves the boy without a school weight room and the father wants his own habit to carry over
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Raised early and with real feeling — 'I'd love for him to be able to kind of, whatever I'm doing, to just kind of carry over to something that we're doing together' — and answered only with a passing 'you can teach kids' inside the education pillar. Whether the programme supports or permits a parent training a minor alongside them is genuinely unclear from anything said.

unmet_demand.want: A back that is made stronger rather than merely protected — he drew the distinction himself between avoidance and rehabilitation
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme claims the mechanism (core, stability, imbalances and compensations seen from movement) but nothing establishes whether a back under active chiropractic care with recurring acute episodes should be doing loaded hip hinges. The answer was deferred until after purchase, to be raised with Trevor.

unmet_demand.want: Rebuilt leg and trunk strength specifically for playing soccer with his son — he can measure the loss in yards on a long ball
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The most tangible performance goal he gave and it was never reflected back or connected to the programming. It did not appear in the rep's otherwise strong five-point summary, and no sport-specific claim was made.
